TASK ID: three-sat-to-independent-set

USER REQUEST:
Write a polynomial-time reduction from 3-SAT to Independent Set. problems.py defines both problems: SOURCE is 3-SAT and TARGET is Independent Set. The SOURCE and TARGET class docstrings give the exact instance formats, yes-conditions and edge cases.

PROBLEM DEFINITIONS (the SOURCE and TARGET docstrings from problems.py, complete as given here):

SOURCE = ThreeSat
3-SAT.

Instance: {"num_vars": m, "clauses": [[l1, l2, l3], ...]}
  * Variables are 1..m. A literal is +v (v is true) or -v (v is false).
  * Every clause has exactly 3 literals on 3 different variables, so a
    clause may not repeat a variable or contain both v and -v.
  * Literal order inside a clause and clause order do not matter. The
    same clause may appear more than once.
  * Variables need not all appear in a clause.

Yes iff some assignment of true/false to variables 1..m makes every
clause contain at least one true literal.

Edge cases: a formula with no clauses is satisfiable (yes), for any m,
including m = 0. A formula with clauses needs m >= 3.

TARGET = IndependentSet
Independent Set.

Instance: {"n": n, "edges": [[u, v], ...], "k": k}
  * Vertices are 0..n-1. Edges are undirected pairs [u, v] with u != v;
    [u, v] and [v, u] are the same edge and may not both appear.
  * k is any integer.

Yes iff the graph has an independent set of AT LEAST k vertices: k
vertices with no edge between any two of them.

Edge cases: k <= 0 is always yes. k > n is always no. With no edges,
every set of vertices is independent.

INPUT FILES: ["problems.py"]
WORKING DIRECTORY: /tmp/reduction-lp9hieoh
All input files are in this directory; run every command from it and write your files here. problems.py is long (about 500 lines): you do not need to read it to know the formats, which are given above. It provides SOURCE and TARGET with is_yes(instance), validate(instance) and random_instance(rng, scale); search it (e.g. with grep) only if you need something specific.

REQUIRED OUTPUT: create reduce.py in the workspace, defining
    reduce(instance) -> instance
It takes an instance of the source problem and returns an instance of the target problem, both in the formats documented in problems.py. The answer to the returned instance must be yes exactly when the answer to the input instance is yes, and reduce must run in polynomial time. Do not call the brute-force solvers inside reduce.

You may read files such as problems.py, but do not run, execute or test any code. Write reduce.py, then submit.
Do not merely describe code: leave the files at those exact paths.
Every reply must contain exactly one bash tool call. When you are done, finish by running exactly: echo COMPLETE_TASK_AND_SUBMIT_FINAL_OUTPUT

"""Polynomial-time reduction from 3-SAT to Independent Set.

Source instance: {"num_vars": m, "clauses": [[l1, l2, l3], ...]}
Target instance: {"n": n, "edges": [[u, v], ...], "k": k}

Construction
------------
For every clause C_i create a triangle on three new vertices, one per
literal occurrence in that clause.  Within a clause every pair of vertices
is joined by an edge, so an independent set contains at most one vertex
from each clause-triangle.

Additionally, for every two vertices in different clause-triangles whose
literals are complementary (one is +v and the other -v for the same
variable v), add an edge between them.  Such a pair cannot both be chosen,
which enforces consistency of the truth assignment represented by the
chosen literals.

Set k equal to the number of clauses.  Any independent set has at most one
vertex per triangle, hence size at most the number of clauses.  Therefore a
set of size at least k exists iff one literal can be selected from every
clause with no complementary pair selected, i.e. iff the formula is
satisfiable (variables that occur in no selected literal may be assigned
arbitrarily).

The graph has 3 * len(clauses) vertices and O(len(clauses)^2) edges, so the
construction runs in polynomial time.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

from typing import Any


def reduce(instance: dict[str, Any]) -> dict[str, Any]:
    """Reduce a 3-SAT instance to an Independent Set instance.

    The returned instance is yes for Independent Set exactly when the input
    is satisfiable.
    """
    clauses = instance["clauses"]
    num_clauses = len(clauses)

    # Vertex 3*i + j corresponds to the j-th literal of clause i.
    n = 3 * num_clauses
    edges: list[list[int]] = []

    # Triangle inside each clause: at most one literal per clause may be
    # chosen.
    for i in range(num_clauses):
        base = 3 * i
        edges.append([base, base + 1])
        edges.append([base, base + 2])
        edges.append([base + 1, base + 2])

    # Conflict edges between complementary literals in different clauses.
    for i in range(num_clauses):
        for j in range(i + 1, num_clauses):
            for a in range(3):
                lit_a = clauses[i][a]
                u = 3 * i + a
                for b in range(3):
                    lit_b = clauses[j][b]
                    if lit_a == -lit_b:
                        v = 3 * j + b
                        edges.append([u, v])

    # One vertex per clause can be chosen; the assignment is satisfiable iff
    # that many mutually non-adjacent vertices exist.
    return {"n": n, "edges": edges, "k": num_clauses}
